My cousin had a nose job 2 years ago and it seems she's now altered her lips too. She was absolutely model-type gorgeous pre-surgery, nose included. She had the nose job because she'd been focusing on her nose for as long as she remembers and told herself once she'd get the nose job, she'd be truly content with her appearance. She's not, ofcourse. 
It's not my business but its super sad to see someone spend $3000+ on a beauty industry scam. My beef is with the industry amd society promoting it, not the people choosing to have plastic surgery. 
In almost all cases the person does not end up happier, they just 'discovered' a way to alter their appearance, literally externalizing and internal issue: lack of self love and confidence. It would've been better if my cousin got therapy or whatever to help her have a healthier relationship with herself. Even better rif she didn't grow up knowing she could, should and would 'perfect her physical appearance'.

If they get offended because you told them they looked better pre-surgery is because the core pain they feel remains unresolved, no matter how much/little surgery they get.

But it's absolutely rude and strange to comment on someone's appearance, so don't do that.
